newsitem.title: USA: Merck, American Home profits jump on rising drug sales.
newsitem.headline: Merck, American Home profits jump on rising drug sales.

text.p: Major pharmaceutical companies Tuesday reported surprisingly high fourth-quarter profits, boosted by strong sales of their new and established brand-name drugs worldwide.
Merck & Co. Inc.'s profits rose 22 percent, American Home Products Inc. said its earnings rose more than sixfold, and Warner-Lambert Co. said its net income rose 39 percent.

"Earnings for the ethical drug companies are going back to levels seen at the start of the decade, except the quality of earnings is better," James Keeney, an analyst at Rodman & Renshaw said. "These are unit-volume driven gains, not driven by double-digit price increases."

Merck's profits rose 22 percent to $1.04 billion in the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $857.8 million in the year-ago period. Earnings per share grew to 87 cents from 70 cents, topping analysts' mean estimate of 86 cents. Sales rose 19 percent to $5.41 billion from $4.56 billion.

"Sales growth for the quarter and the year was led by established major products, 1995 and 1996 product introductions and growth from the Merck-Medco Managed Care business," said Merck Chairman Raymond Gilmartin.
For the year, the Whitehouse Station, N.J.-based company's net income grew 16 percent to $3.88 billion, or $3.20 a share. Sales jumped 19 percent to $19.83 billion.

Merck attributed its strong performance to the popularity of its cholesterol-lowering agents, Zocor and Mevacor, which dominate over 40 percent of the market sector worldwide. Zocor, which aims to prevent heart attacks in people with high cholesterol, accounted for 14 percent of sales for 1996.

Fosamax, Merck's nonhormonal medicine for the treatment of osteoporosis in postmenopausal women, was introduced in 47 countries in 1996, with more than 1.3 million patients receiving the drug worldwide, the company said.
"Merck did extremely well in the quarter," said Jack Lamberton, an analyst at NatWest Securities. "The company had strong top-line growth and controlled expenses, which was a bit of a surprise."

American Home Products Inc. said profits, bolstered especially by its anti-obesity drug Redux, rose to $511.6 million, or 80 cents a share, in the fourth quarter, from $81.7 million, or 13 cents a share, a year ago. This exceeded analysts' estimates of 78 cents a share.
Revenues rose to $3.48 billion from $3.33 billion.
For the year, earnings rose to $1.88 billion, or $2.96 a share, from $1.68 billion, or $2.71 a share. Revenues rose to $14.09 billion from $13.38 billion.
The Madison, N.J.-based health care products company said U.S. drug sales rose 15 percent for the fourth quarter, primarily due to higher sales of Redux and the oestrogen replacement drug Premarin.

U.S. consumer health care sales fell 6 percent for the quarter amid lower sales of over-the-counter pain medications Orudis KT and Advil. There were higher sales of anti-acid Axid AR and Centrum vitamins.

Morris Plains, N.J.-based Warner-Lambert Co. said its net income rose to $171.0 million in the quarter ended Dec. 31 from $123.1 million in the year-ago period. Earnings per share rose to 63 cents from 45 cents, surpassing analysts' forecasts of 62 cents. Sales edged down 1 percent to $1.84 billion from $1.86 billion.
Full-year 1996 net income rose 6 percent to $786.5 million, or $2.90 a share. Sales rose to a record $7.23 billion from $7.04 billion.

"As a result of the successful discovery and development of innovative new products, we believe Warner-Lambert is poised to enter a sustained period of unprecedented growth," Chairman Melvin Goodes said.
Merck's stock rose $2.25 to $86.75, American Home gained 50 cents to $60.25 and Warner-Lambert rose $12.5 cents to $73.75 on the New York Stock Exchange in early afternoon trading.
